Accessibility Audit:

The text uses outdated and non-inclusive language by referring to "the blind." This is a form of person-first language violation and can be considered offensive. The preferred terminology is "people who are blind" or "visually impaired individuals," depending on the specific context and individual preference. Additionally, the phrase "ensure they can navigate" assumes a monolithic experience for all blind people. A more inclusive approach would be to state that the design supports independent navigation for people with visual impairments.

Recommended revision: "Our new office building has been designed with people who are blind in mind; we have tactile floor plans and audio descriptions at every point of interest to support independent navigation and confidence for all visitors."

The color of a common crow is black.
